conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: Program-address-identifier
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.4.3.13.3 'Literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal whose length is not zero.' OK. Probed: "" -> COBOLNET2157 (zero length); SPACE (figurative) -> COBOLNET2157; B"1" (boolean) -> COBOLNET2157; 123 (numeric) -> parse error COBOL0308; X"41" (alphanumeric hex), "A" & "B" (concatenation, 8.8.3.3 GR3) and N"PAISUB" (national) accepted. No existing negative golden exercises SR2 -> test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the program-pointer family; absent from COBOL-85 - Annex E covers only 2014->2023, the introduction is the 2002 address-identifier; probe: --std 85 draws COBOLNET0900)]
rows.rule-text: Literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal whose length is not zero.

rows.subject: Program-address-identifier
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.4.3.13.3 'Program-prototype-name-1 shall be a program prototype specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph.' OK. The prototype arm is taken only when host.ProgramPrototypes (the REPOSITORY program-specifier table) holds the word; otherwise the word must resolve as identifier-1. Probed: undeclared NOTDECL -> COBOLNET1639 + COBOLNET2157 naming SR3/SR1; declared PAIPA/PAIPB resolve (g3/g5). The pb549 golden covers only the positive arm; no negative golden for an undeclared prototype -> test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the program-pointer family; absent from COBOL-85 - Annex E covers only 2014->2023, the introduction is the 2002 address-identifier; probe: --std 85 draws COBOLNET0900)]
rows.rule-text: Program-prototype-name-1 shall be a program prototype specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph.

rows.subject: Program-address-identifier
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.4.3.13.3 'This identifier format shall not be specified as a receiving operand.' OK. Enforced structurally: programAddressIdentifier is referenced only from sender slots (setProgramAddressStatement's TO operand; addressIdentifier in CALL/INVOKE arguments and comparisonOperand). CALL BY REFERENCE of an address-identifier is a SENDING operand (cite.py --check 14.9.4.3 'if identifier-2 is an address-identifier, identifier-2 is a sending operand' OK). Probed: `SET ADDRESS OF PROGRAM "X" TO PP` -> COBOL0201; `MOVE PP TO ADDRESS OF PROGRAM "X"` -> COBOLNET0901; `INITIALIZE ADDRESS OF PROGRAM "X"` -> COBOLNET0901. No negative golden -> test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the program-pointer family; absent from COBOL-85 - Annex E covers only 2014->2023, the introduction is the 2002 address-identifier; probe: --std 85 draws COBOLNET0900)]
rows.rule-text: This identifier format shall not be specified as a receiving operand.

rows.subject: Program-address-identifier
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.4.3.13.4 'For a COBOL program, the address is that of the outermost program identified by the externalized program-name in its PROGRAM-ID paragraph.' OK (GR2). EntryOf matches only ParentPath==null nodes (outermost) on Node.CallName (externalized; PB303); the prototype arm resolves through proto.ExternalizedName. Probed: a literal naming the CONTAINED program PAINEST -> NULL (NEST-NULL, probe ok2) - the outermost half. conformance:2002/pb549_program_address_identifier arm 4 pins only the externalized-name half (PB549P AS "PB549X"), so it cannot close both halves; test-needed: a golden taking ADDRESS OF PROGRAM of a nested program-name and showing NULL. Non-COBOL half: implementor-defined, Annex A item 142 is conditionally required upon non-COBOL support; COBOL.NET declares no CALL-CONVENTION directive and no non-COBOL program can be declared (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-19 says the same), so the condition is not met. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the program-pointer family; absent from COBOL-85 - Annex E covers only 2014->2023, the introduction is the 2002 address-identifier; probe: --std 85 draws COBOLNET0900)]
rows.rule-text: The program may be written in COBOL or in another language for which the implementor has declared support. For a COBOL program, the address is that of the outermost program identified by the externalized program-name in its PROGRAM-ID paragraph. For a non-COBOL program, the relation between the address and the associated program is defined by the implementor.

rows.subject: Program-address-identifier
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.4.3.13.4 'has the characteristics of a program-pointer restricted to program-prototype-name-1' OK (GR3). BoundProgramAddress carries Prototype=word only for the prototype arm; BindSetProgramAddress compares it with a restricted receiver under 14.9.39.3 SR22. Probed (g3/g3b/g5): receiver `TYPE RPT` (RPT = PROGRAM-POINTER TO PAIPA TYPEDEF) with ADDRESS OF PROGRAM PAIPB (2 formals vs 1) -> COBOLNET1959 citing GR3; with literal "PAIPA" -> COBOLNET1959 (unrestricted sender); with ADDRESS OF PROGRAM PAIPA -> compiles and CALL RP USING X1 displays 'PA Z'. No existing golden drives the ADDRESS OF PROGRAM prototype arm against a restricted receiver (pb817 uses the TO ENTRY extension) -> test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the program-pointer family; absent from COBOL-85 - Annex E covers only 2014->2023, the introduction is the 2002 address-identifier; probe: --std 85 draws COBOLNET0900)]
rows.rule-text: When program-prototype-name-1 is specified, the program-address-identifier has the characteristics of a program-pointer restricted to program-prototype-name-1.

rows.subject: Qualification
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.4.2.2.1 "the names of any group items superordinate to both the data-name and the subject of the data description entry clause are used as implicit qualifiers" -> OK §8.4.2.2.1 5). EntryClauseCandidates walks the subject's ancestors innermost-first and returns the candidate set under the FIRST group that holds any candidate (every survivor there shares the same implicit qualifiers, so two survivors stay ambiguous), falling back to the scope-wide QualifiedCandidates set; explicit qualifiers are still applied by QualifierChainMatches. Callers: OCCURS DEPENDING ON and SAME AS - the data description entry clauses whose operand is a data-name that can share a group with the subject (OCCURS KEY resolves within the table's own subtree; RENAMES is level 66 and never subordinate; REDEFINES is rule 2; VALIDATE-module clauses and SELECT WHEN are declined modules). BOTH HALVES PROBED (pinned cobol.exe, --run): d1 - G1{CNT=2, T ODO CNT}, G2{CNT=3, T ODO CNT}, G{A{CNT=2}, B{CNT=4}, T ODO CNT OF B}, H{HB{CNT=3}, HA{CNT=1, HT ODO CNT}} -> D1=3,4,6,2 at --std 85 and 2023 (spec-derived: 1+2, 1+3, 1+1+4, 1+1 - each unqualified CNT implicitly qualified by the shared group; the explicit CNT OF B supplies the within-group uniqueness). d2 - G{A{CNT}, B{CNT}, T ODO CNT} -> COBOLNET1639 '2 declarations match' at 85 (implicit qualifier G does not establish uniqueness within the group, so the explicit qualifier the rule requires is demanded). d3 (SAME AS, 2014/2023) - G1{S X(3), U SAME AS S}, G2{S X(5), U SAME AS S} -> D3=3,5. Out of scope and noted: report group description entries are a distinct entry kind from data description entries (§13.15; the standard lists 'a data description entry, a report group description entry, or a screen description entry' separately), so SOURCE/SUM references to same-report sum counters are not this rule's population (see dossier_gaps for the unregistered SOURCE-of-a-sum-counter lead). No golden pins the implicit-qualifier leg (pb885_odo_depending_qualified / pb978 write EXPLICIT qualifiers across records), so test-ref is empty. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the implicit-qualifier rule governs data description entry clauses in every edition; the OCCURS DEPENDING leg exists at 85, the SAME AS leg only where SAME AS exists, 2014+)]
rows.rule-text: The name is a data-name referenced in a data description entry clause whose subject is subordinate to the same group item as that data-name. In this case, the names of any group items superordinate to both the data-name and the subject of the data description entry clause are used as implicit qualifiers for the reference, in addition to any explicit qualifiers needed to establish uniqueness within that group.

rows.subject: RAISE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: "Identifier-1 is a sending operand." (cite.py --check 14.9.29.3 -> OK §14.9.29.3 3)). BindRaise resolves identifier-1 through ResolveSending (the sending-operand chokepoint), and EmitRaiseObject only READS it (PlaceRenderer.Read) into ExceptionState.SetObject. EXCEPTION-OBJECT itself (a predefined reference that may not be a receiving operand, §8.4.3.6.3 SR1) is accepted as identifier-1 (probe/raise/sr2b.cob prints the handler line for `RAISE EXCEPTION-OBJECT`), consistent with sending-only use. No test asserts sending-ness specifically -> test-needed.

rows.subject: RAISE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: "Within an exception-checking PERFORM statement, the RAISE statement shall not be specified in any imperative statement other than imperative-statement-1." (cite.py --check 14.9.29.3 -> OK §14.9.29.3 4)). Region D = every WHEN-phrase statementBlock plus FINALLY; a descendant sweep emits COBOLNET1611. Probe probe/raise/sr4.cob (RAISE in WHEN EC-SIZE, WHEN OTHER and FINALLY) -> COBOLNET1611 citing SR4; RAISE in imperative-statement-1 is accepted (conformance-test:PerformFormat3Tests.RaiseInImp1_Accepted_NoBan pins the accept half). Observations, not verdict-changing: the diagnostic is anchored at the PERFORM's position (8,12), not the RAISE's line, and the three violations print once; a RAISE inside a nested inline PERFORM inside a WHEN phrase is caught (descendant sweep), which is the literal reading. No test asserts the REJECT half (no *Rejected1611 test exists) -> test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 2023 (the exception-checking PERFORM is new in 2023, E.3.3 item 36 / VCR row 79)]
rows.rule-text: Within an exception-checking PERFORM statement, the RAISE statement shall not be specified in any imperative statement other than imperative-statement-1.

rows.subject: RECORD clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 GR7 (Format 2 variable-length; integer-2 min, integer-3 max). `RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 5 TO 20 DEPENDING ON L` - L=3 and L=21 answer 44, L=7 writes a 7-byte record (4-byte prefix + 7, p4.dat 11 bytes), READ restores L=7 (probe/record-clause/p4.cob); REWRITE with L=30 answers 44. Variable-length framing on sequential/relative/indexed via RecordFraming. Integer-2 = 0 is covered by conformance:2023/pb721_zero_length_record (min half only), so no single spec-derived test pins both bounds -> test-ref left empty.
rows.rule-text: Format 2 is used to specify variable-length records. Integer-2 specifies the minimum number of bytes to be contained in any record of the file. Integer-3 specifies the maximum number of bytes in any record of the file.

rows.subject: RECORD clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 'the execution of a DELETE, RELEASE, REWRITE, START, or WRITE statement or the unsuccessful execution of a READ or RETURN statement does not alter the content' OK (GR12). Every verb probed: WRITE (L=3/21/7 kept, probe/record-clause/p4.cob), REWRITE (L=30 kept, p4.cob), unsuccessful sequential READ at end (L=99 kept, p4.cob), indexed START (L=77 kept), unsuccessful keyed READ status 23 (L=77 kept), DELETE (L=55 kept) (p5.cob), RELEASE (L=05 and 01 kept, p6.cob), RETURN AT END (L=88 kept, p6.cob). No single spec-derived test pins all eight -> test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: If data-name-1 is specified, the execution of a DELETE, RELEASE, REWRITE, START, or WRITE statement or the unsuccessful execution of a READ or RETURN statement does not alter the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1.

rows.subject: RECORD clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 'the size of each record is completely defined in the record description entry' OK (GR18). integer-4/5 are the connector's min/max (F3 ODO record: 4 bytes -> 44, 24 bytes -> 44, 12 bytes -> 00, probe/record-clause/p4.cob); each record is written at its own description's size (A3 5 bytes, B3 10 bytes, p3.cob) with no DEPENDING item. RecordClauseRules deliberately adds no SR4-analogue for Format 3 (p7.cob F3 with a 50-byte record under CONTAINS 5 TO 30 compiles clean - the standard states no such rule). || Code-location detail (moved from the field by registrar 14e): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/RecordClauseRules.cs (no SR4 analogue for Format 3) || Re-sited by registrar 14e: the RecordClauseRules.cs witness was removed because that table has no row for this rule (RecordClauseRuleDriftTests clamp: a code-location naming RecordClauseRules claims a Catalog row). RecordClauseRules.Screen only CONSUMES FileModel.Min/MaxRecordSize.
rows.rule-text: When format 3 of the RECORD clause is used, integer-4 and integer-5 refer to the minimum number of bytes in the smallest size record and the maximum number of bytes in the largest size record, respectively. However, in this case, the size of each record is completely defined in the record description entry.

rows.subject: RECORD clause (whether fixed or variable records produced for fixed-or-variable-length format)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §13.18.43.4 GR17 (cite.py OK 17)) leaves fixed vs variable to the implementor. Code: DataBinder.BindRecordClause (DataBinder.cs:1686-1714) binds a TO-without-VARYING clause as file.Varying = VaryingRecordInfo(lo, hi, dep, VaryingClause: false) - the variable-length model. Probe probe/f3.cob at --std 85 and 2023: sequential file = 05000000 'ABCDE' 0A000000 'ABCDEFGHIJ' (23 bytes); relative file = header then the same two prefixed frames; both editions identical. No golden distinguishes fixed from variable for format 3 (pb721_zero_length_record F3 reads back its record but cannot tell), so Pinned by is empty. Owning note kb/Work PB1278 (open; this row discharges its item-148 half, the item-146 half stays open behind PB1276).
rows.rule-text: RECORD clause (whether fixed or variable records produced for fixed-or-variable-length format). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (13.18.43, RECORD clause, General rule 17)
